newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Costello warns of drought-led slide in GDP.
newsitem.headline: Costello warns of drought-led slide in GDP.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello warned on Friday that the El Nino weather pattern threatened to bring on a drought that would depress farm output and force GDP growth lower than budget forecasts.
"One of the largest risks surrounding the forecasts for farm production is the development of below average rainfall," Costello said in a speech to the Economic Society of Australia.

He said the government had been warned by the Bureau of Meterology that current El Nino weather patterns could bring on a severe drought affecting production from Australia's wool, wheat and beef farms.
"Weather conditions data also indicated that the event is the strongest since the episode of 1982/83, a period of widespread drought in Australia," he said.

"Lower than forecast farm product would lead to lower GDP growth in 1997/98, but it is too early to change the forecast because the timing, distribution and amount of rainfall over the next few weeks will be critical in determining the farm production ultimately achieved," he said.
The government forecast in the budget that farm product would fall two percent in the year to June 30, 1998 and that overall GDP would grow 3.75 percent.

The government's forecast was already below most market forecasts, which are grouped around four percent for the 1997/98 year. The Reserve Bank of Australia said in May it expected GDP growth of about four percent in calendar 1997.
